APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING
  OF FEBRUARY 19, 2019

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 5:09 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Jerry Velasco, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – absent
  Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Councilmember Ancona  4-0 (Councilmember Martinez Muela absent)

4.  CLOSED SESSION (5:00 p.m. – 6:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 5:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 6:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 6:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 6:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 and 4.2.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 5:10 p.m. Councilmember Martinez Muela joined the City Council in
  Closed Session.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 6:02 p.m.

  City Attorney Rick Olivarez reported out of Closed Session with respect to Items
  4.1 and 4.2.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  2
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of February 19, 2019

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Fenglan Liu – I just noticed that the Notice is defective so I request that the City of El
  Monte cancel these two projects today and correct the hearing notice and give a correct

  property owner you list here as Crown East Holding, LLC. Actually this company doesn’t
  exist this property was transferred to JP Ventures, LLC so this notice that the City of El
  Monte put in L.A. Times is defective.

  Andrew Liebernack – I live on Gate Avenue where the Christmas lights and party is held
  every year for the kids in the community. I used to be really involved up to 10 years ago
  when things changed. I am concerned about all the homeless people I see everywhere.
  I am concerned about the conditions of our streets, I am concerned about the graffiti that
  is not being removed. City Managers and other department heads come and go.
  There’s no process being done.

  Maria Morgan – I’m a resident of El Monte and I wanted to just make a public comment I
  know I have reached out to a few of you thanking the City Council for the bulk drop-off
  event that was a couple of weeks ago. I did want to thank our Public Works for their hard
  work on that Saturday because it was raining. We also had our Police Explores that
  were there. I also wanted to make an extra request if there is any way possible to have
  an extra one because since it was rainy day I am not sure how many residents were
  able to go and participate.

  My name is Ellis Raskin, I'm an attorney here representing the Greater Los Angeles
  Communities Alliance. Tonight I want to talk specifically about two reasons why you
  have a legally mandated duty to not approve this project tonight. First, we're operating
  tonight under the assumption that the City's permitting procedures are legal when, in
  fact, they are preempted and illegal under the Controlled Substances Act. Second, the
  environmental review that was conducted for this project falls substantially short of the
  legally mandated requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act. So, as you
  know, under federal law, marijuana is not legal. There is no exception for medical use.
  Therefore, by approving project permits and entitlements for these marijuana facilities,
  and by engaging in this permitting process, this City is authorizing use that directly
  conflicts with federal law.

  Zig Jiang – It is a great pleasure to have an opportunity to speak out my concerns. I
  Just as you know were here to oppose any marijuana projects in the City of El Monte.

  Ken Meng – I am president of the Greater Los Angeles Community Alliance at
  greatlaca.org. We oppose the marijuana projects.

  Sharon Liao – The applicants state that the trash is safe, but I have study and then we
  can see recently that a lot of newspaper and TV and then my report from fire safety
  official claims at least 10 fires, explosions have occurred.

  David Mcglothin – I’m a resident of El Monte northern part. I opposite the project strictly
  on a moral value.

  Lui Ma – Tonight I am here, I beg your mercy. Please pass these two projects. I
  strongly support because humanitarian purpose.

  Sam Meng – Since the Council wants to focus on the facts I’ll do that. The chief of
  police mentioned Desert Hot Springs. The population there is 29,000 as of the last two
  years. El Monte’s population is about four times of that and is the center of the San
  Gabriel Valley. The impact cannot be compared to that. At the informational meeting
  the City held on Saturday to explain the benefits of medical marijuana, I am informed of
  both sides, but realize some key facts not mentioned.

  Irma Zamorano – I’ve been a resident of El Monte for 48 years and I’m here because I
  strongly oppose the marijuana facilities. Since the proposed sites are too close to the
  schools there is little doubt that these facilities will pose high risk to ur young generation
  physically and psychological.

  Ferry Soendjojo – I strongly oppose the approval for another medicinal cannabis facility
  while the first project has brought lawsuit against our City at the cost of the taxpayer
  money.

  Kewei Zhao – I actually have two questions about Ms. Donavanik’s presentation. As the
  project had been labeled as medicinal use, but I think it is very vaguely used because
  medicinal is something that needs oversight.

  Jacqueline Morales – I am here to say that I am for the proposed projects.

  Fenglan Liu – I’m a resident of Temple City. I’m talking on behalf of more than 20,000
  residents, local residents from City of El Monte and the City of Temple City who oppose
  the projects.

  Larry Fry – As I brought up at a previous Council meeting last year, I believe no matter
  what side you side with in this whole marijuana industry, it’s your opinion. I think our
  Council should have this issue placed on a ballot measure. This way our voting
